content.text:
In the installed `agents` 0.27.0 you can't pass storage to the constructor. Its signature is `new MCPClientManager(name, version, options?)`, and `MCPClientManagerOptions` only accepts `env` (used to restore `rpc://` connections) and `createAuthProvider` (a factory for OAuth). See `node_modules/agents/dist/agent-routing-Bhdbvf7s.d.ts:2743` and `:2799`.

`MCPClientManager` is a `LifecycleCapability`, so it uses the storage of whichever Lifecycle host installs it. Inside an `Agent`, that's the agent's own Durable Object storage, available as `this.mcp`. To have it use your own `DurableObjectStorage`, install it on a Lifecycle in your own Durable Object, and it will use that object's `ctx.storage`. The type comments mark installing it directly on a Lifecycle (outside `agent.mcp`) as experimental. The older pattern of passing `{ storage }` to the constructor no longer exists in this version.

In the installed `agents` 0.27.0 you can't pass storage to the constructor. Its signature is `new MCPClientManager(name, version, options?)`, and `MCPClientManagerOptions` only accepts `env` (used to restore `rpc://` connections) and `createAuthProvider` (a factory for OAuth). See `node_modules/agents/dist/agent-routing-Bhdbvf7s.d.ts:2743` and `:2799`.

`MCPClientManager` is a `LifecycleCapability`, so it uses the storage of whichever Lifecycle host installs it. Inside an `Agent`, that's the agent's own Durable Object storage, available as `this.mcp`. To have it use your own `DurableObjectStorage`, install it on a Lifecycle in your own Durable Object, and it will use that object's `ctx.storage`. The type comments mark installing it directly on a Lifecycle (outside `agent.mcp`) as experimental. The older pattern of passing `{ storage }` to the constructor no longer exists in this version.
